prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” interior painting company for everyone — the right company depends on your home, budget, timeline, and quality expectations. I can help you find the best one for your specific job. A quick plan:

1) Quick questions
- Is this residential or commercial?
- How many rooms / approximate square footage?
- Any special needs (historic home, lead paint, popcorn ceiling removal, trim/cabinet painting)?
- Budget range and desired start date?

2) How to find top candidates in St. Louis
- Search Google Maps, Yelp, Angi, Houzz and the BBB for “interior painters St. Louis” and filter by high ratings and many recent reviews.
- Check local Facebook community groups for personal recommendations.
- Look for companies that display credentials and insurance info on their site and have many before/after photos.

3) Who to consider (types)
- Reputable national/franchise options with local branches (e.g., CertaPro Painters, Five Star Painting) — good for consistent processes and warranties.
- Well-reviewed local independent painters — often more personalized and sometimes better value.
I can pull up current local options if you want me to search (I’ll need permission to access the web or you can paste a few names you found).

4) What to ask every painter (checklist)
- Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide proof (COI)?
- Are you lead-safe certified (if house built before 1978)?
- Do you provide written, itemized estimates? (Include prep, number of coats, paint brand & sheen, and cleanup.)
- What surface prep is included (sanding, priming, patching drywall, caulking trim)?
- What paint brand and warranty do you use? Do you include primer?
- Timeline: start date, days on site, projected completion.
- Payment schedule and accepted methods.
- Request references and photos of similar past jobs.
- What’s your policy for change orders and punch-list items?

5) Pricing guidance (very rough)
- Single room (12x12) interior repaint often runs from $300–$1,200 depending on prep and paint quality.
- Whole-house interior repaint commonly ranges $2,500–$10,000+ depending on size, trim, ceilings and condition.
Get three written bids for apples-to-apples comparison.

6) How to choose
- Favor clear, itemized bids over low-ballers.
- Choose a contractor who communicates well, has positive recent references, and provides a written contract and warranty.
- Verify insurance and (if applicable) lead-safe certification before work begins.

If you want, tell me your answers to the questions in (1), or paste 3 painter names you’re considering and I’ll help compare them and draft a message to request bids.
